feedbackActionPlan.summary: Add a selectable 12.2 mm diameter option for pro shafts and carry that choice through validation, pricing, order review, and shop-facing manufacturing notation.
feedbackActionPlan.customerImpact: Customers who prefer a smaller pro shaft diameter can order 12.2 mm directly instead of using notes or contacting the shop, reducing order friction and misinterpretation risk.
feedbackActionPlan.businessImpact: The option can capture more custom pro shaft orders with low catalog complexity, but it must be represented consistently so pricing, order records, and build sheets stay accurate.
feedbackActionPlan.confidence: The raw request is direct and unambiguous. Confidence is reduced because this checkout appears to contain a Rust billiards simulation rather than the website/configurator implementation, so file-level surfaces are inferred from standard ecommerce configurator patterns.

researchFindings.finding: The source feedback asks specifically for a 12.2 mm option for pro shafts, not for all shaft families or every diameter selector.

No website, storefront, product data, or order-form implementation was surfaced in this checkout under the expected application paths; the implementation plan assumes those artifacts exist in a separate website checkout.
Model the value as a numeric millimeter diameter, 12.2, and render it as 12.2 mm everywhere to avoid inconsistent strings such as 12.20, 12.2mm, or 12-2.

The change must propagate beyond the visible dropdown: validation, price calculation, cart/order summary, stored order payloads, admin review, and manufacturing/build-sheet notation all need the same canonical value.

implementationPlan.step: Locate the canonical pro shaft product option source, such as a product-options data file, CMS entry, schema enum, or configurator constant that currently lists allowed pro shaft diameters.
Add 12.2 as an allowed diameter only for pro shafts unless product leadership confirms it should apply to other shaft types.
Use a single canonical representation for the option: internal value 12.2, unit mm, customer label 12.2 mm, and manufacturing label Pro shaft diameter: 12.2 mm.
Update frontend option rendering so the 12.2 mm choice appears in the pro shaft diameter selector in the same order as adjacent diameters, preferably numeric ascending order.
Update client-side and server-side validation to accept 12.2 for pro shaft diameter while continuing to reject unsupported diameters and invalid shaft-family combinations.
Update pricing rules so 12.2 mm uses the default pro shaft diameter price unless the business explicitly assigns an upcharge; do not create a silent surcharge.
Update cart, checkout, confirmation email, customer order summary, admin order view, and export payloads so the selected diameter displays as 12.2 mm.
Update downstream manufacturing notation, build sheets, labels, and any CSV/print/export templates to show 12.2 mm as a required pro shaft diameter specification.
Add focused coverage for option availability, validation acceptance, pricing default behavior, order summary display, and manufacturing/export notation for a pro shaft configured at 12.2 mm.
If option values are cached or synced from a CMS, refresh the relevant cache/index and confirm the storefront and admin surfaces read from the same canonical source.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A customer configuring a pro shaft can select 12.2 mm from the diameter options without using a free-text note.
The 12.2 mm option is not shown for unrelated shaft families unless intentionally enabled there.
Client-side and server-side validation both accept 12.2 mm for pro shafts and reject malformed values such as 12.2 without the expected unit metadata if the schema requires units.
Choosing 12.2 mm preserves the default pro shaft price unless a documented price rule says otherwise.
The cart, checkout review, confirmation email, customer order summary, and admin order detail all display 12.2 mm consistently.
The manufacturing/build-sheet output includes an explicit 12.2 mm pro shaft diameter notation that cannot be confused with tip size, joint diameter, or taper.

risks.risk: If diameter options are duplicated across frontend, backend, and manufacturing templates, adding only the visible selector can create orders the shop cannot build from reliably.
If 12.2 mm requires a different taper, tooling limit, or warranty rule, using default pricing and default manufacturing instructions may be incomplete.
If the order schema stores diameter as a string, inconsistent formatting can break analytics, exports, or fulfillment filters.

openQuestions.question: Should 12.2 mm be available for every pro shaft material/construction variant, or only specific pro shaft SKUs?
Does 12.2 mm carry the same price and lead time as existing pro shaft diameters?
Should the manufacturing notation distinguish tip diameter from any separate joint diameter or taper measurement on the same order?
